```{=html}
<div class="teaching-demo" id="breadboard-explorer" data-demo="breadboard" role="region" aria-labelledby="breadboard-demo-title">
  <div class="demo-heading"><div><p class="demo-eyebrow">Try it · Follow the hidden connections</p><h3 id="breadboard-demo-title" class="unnumbered">Which holes are connected?</h3></div><button type="button" data-fullscreen hidden>Enlarge demo</button></div>
  <p>Click a hole to reveal every hole connected to it. Add a jumper to join two groups, or test a pair of holes for continuity.</p>
  <div class="breadboard-workbench" hidden>
    <div class="breadboard-controls">
      <div>
        <label for="breadboard-mode">What do you want to do?</label>
        <select id="breadboard-mode"><option value="inspect">Inspect connections</option><option value="wire">Add a jumper wire</option><option value="test">Test two holes</option></select>
        <p id="breadboard-instruction">Choose a hole to highlight its connected group.</p>
        <button type="button" id="breadboard-cancel" hidden>Cancel first endpoint</button>
      </div>
      <div class="breadboard-options">
        <label><input type="checkbox" id="breadboard-metal" checked> Show metal strips</label>
        <label><input type="checkbox" id="breadboard-split" checked> Split power rails halfway</label>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="breadboard-view">
      <div class="breadboard-scroll" tabindex="0" role="group" aria-label="Interactive breadboard" aria-describedby="breadboard-keyboard">
        <div class="breadboard-board" id="breadboard-board">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 696 484" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
            <rect x="2" y="2" width="692" height="480" rx="18" class="bb-body"></rect>
            <rect x="111" y="44" width="474" height="406" rx="12" class="bb-terminal-area"></rect>
            <rect x="328" y="70" width="40" height="358" rx="10" class="bb-trench"></rect>
            <g id="breadboard-markings"></g>
            <g id="breadboard-strips"></g>
            <g id="breadboard-wires"></g>
          </svg>
          <div id="breadboard-holes" role="group" aria-label="Breadboard holes"></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <p class="breadboard-legend"><span><i class="bb-key-connected"></i>Connected group</span><span><i class="bb-key-selected"></i>Selected hole / probe A</span><span><b>B</b> Second probe</span></p>
      <p id="breadboard-keyboard" class="demo-note">Keyboard: Tab to the board, then to a hole; use arrow keys to move and Enter or Space to select. Escape cancels a first endpoint. On a small screen, scroll the board sideways.</p>
    </div>
      <div class="breadboard-reading" role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
        <strong id="breadboard-result">a3 · 5 connected holes</strong>
        <p id="breadboard-detail">a3–e3 share one metal strip.</p>
        <p id="breadboard-action"></p>
      </div>
      <div class="breadboard-jumpers"><div class="breadboard-jumper-heading"><strong>Jumper wires <span id="breadboard-wire-count">(0)</span></strong><button type="button" id="breadboard-clear" disabled>Clear wires</button></div><p id="breadboard-empty" class="demo-note">No jumpers yet. Wires connect only at their ends; crossing wires do not join.</p><ol id="breadboard-wire-list" aria-label="Jumper wires"></ol></div>
  </div>
  <div class="breadboard-examples" hidden><p><strong>Load an example</strong> <span class="demo-note">(replaces your jumpers)</span></p><div class="demo-presets"><button type="button" data-breadboard-example="row">Five-hole row</button><button type="button" data-breadboard-example="gap">Across the gap</button><button type="button" data-breadboard-example="bridge">Bridge the gap</button><button type="button" data-breadboard-example="rail">Split rail</button></div></div>
  <details class="demo-explanation"><summary>What is connected inside a breadboard?</summary><p>For each numbered row, a–e form one group of five and f–j form another. The centre gap separates the two groups. The next numbered row is a different group, even within the same lettered column.</p><p>Each side rail runs lengthwise, separately from the other rails. On a board with split rails, the upper and lower sections are separate too; a jumper can join them. Actual boards vary: check continuity on your unpowered board with a multimeter.</p></details>
  <p class="demo-note">A shortened, 10-row teaching model. The + and − marks are labels, not voltage sources. This demo models metal connections and ideal jumper wires, not component behaviour, voltage or current. Each hole accepts one jumper end.</p>
  <div class="demo-footer"><span><strong>Try this:</strong> Test a3 and j3. Add a jumper from e3 to f3, then test again. What changed?</span><button type="button" data-reset hidden>Reset</button></div>
  <noscript><p>Enable JavaScript to use the breadboard controls. The explanation above and the wiring diagram below show the internal connections.</p></noscript>
</div>
```
